text:
maria: Quick follow-up on last week's quant RFC — we need an agreed-on packing format + runtime API for model variants (FP8/INT8/4bit) before we start rolling Dedicated. Main tension: single monolithic blob for weights vs per-tensor metadata to enable graceful fallback and recalibration. Thoughts?

jonah: Single blob is attractive for RPC throughput but it really complicates fallbacks. We should include per-tensor metadata (scale/zero-point/qbits) and a small lookup table so the runtime can swap precision per-op.

kai: Agree with per-tensor meta. Also strongly recommend adding provenance (calibration dataset hash + tool version) so we can detect silent quality regressions when calibration drifts. We ran into that in a PoC.

priya: From the runtime/allocator POV, per-tensor metadata increases metadata pressure for tiny models (lots of small tensors). We can mitigate by packing the table and keeping an index (tensor -> offset) so we only touch entries when needed.

maria: Draft proposal idea: header v1 contains {model_id, quant_scheme, calib_hash, kernel_hint, magic, version}. Followed by a compressed meta table with rows: {tensor_name, qbits, scale, zero_point, weight_offset, weight_length}. Compression: LZ4 for fast decode. Backcompat: if table missing treat artifact as legacy fp32. Example header snippet: ```
MAGIC: 0x52455851
VERSION: 1
SCHEME: per-tensor
CALIB_HASH: e3b0c442...
```

quant-bot: Automated check suggestion: on upload validate header.magic and table_crc. Emit warning if calib_hash missing. Add optional 'hotpatch' flag that lets ops ship small per-tensor overrides without rewriting weights.

jonah: Also need a clear runtime API shape. Proposal: `load_model(path, allowed_precisions=["fp32","fp8","int8","4bit"], fallback_order=[...])` returns a ModelDescriptor that contains available_precisions and a per-op mapping to precision. That gives platform code a programmatic knob.

kai: For quality gating, add a tiny eval hook that runs a short validation set at load time if calib_hash changed or allowed_precisions includes lower bits. Log token-level delta (perplexity / logprob) and surface an advisory. If delta > threshold fail the load or flip to safer precision.

priya: Operationally we need a controller-level policy: e.g., a route policy to prefer lower precision when tail latency > SLO. Controller calls `runtime.set_precision_policy(route, policy)` and runtime will consult ModelDescriptor to pick best compatible mapping.

maria: Action items and owners: 1) Packing schema doc (I'll draft) 2) ModelDescriptor proto (jonah) 3) Runtime API PR + allowed_precisions (priya) 4) Mini validation harness and drift sim (kai). Target: end of week for spikes. :calendar:

jonah: +1 — I'll sketch the proto and include migration hints for older artifacts (fallback to fp32 if fields absent).

kai: I'll mock the small eval and a perf script to simulate precision tradeoffs and calibration drift (perturb scales by +-5%).

priya: I'll wire policy hooks into the controller. Will open a short RFC for ops semantics and emergency rollback semantics.

maria: Thanks team — I'll create the follow-up RFC and link this thread. Who wants to pair on header byte layout and magic numbers? @jonah @priya

jonah: Happy to pair tomorrow 11am PT.

priya: Works for me.

maria: Great; I'll add meeting invite and a tiny spec draft to the RFC.

(quick notes: avoid embedding big per-tensor strings in the hotpath. prefer index+offset. be explicit about CRC/compat checks so we don't ship broken artifacts.)
